original_question: Classify normal affine equivariant embeddings of connected solvable linear algebraic groups for which all isotropy groups are semisimple.
target_in_paper: Problem 4: "Classify normal affine equivariant embeddings of connected solvable linear algebraic groups for which all isotropy groups are semisimple. It seems to be easy when maximal tori have dimension one."
correct_elements: Your draft matches the core of the paper's official formulation almost verbatim. It correctly identifies the classification target (normal affine equivariant embeddings), the class of acting groups (connected solvable linear algebraic groups), and the stabilizer condition (all isotropy groups are semisimple).
missing_details: The paper states this as Problem 4, not as a theorem or conjecture.
The official formulation includes the additional remark: "It seems to be easy when maximal tori have dimension one."
The base field is not specified in Problem 4, so a stand-alone version should either name a ground field or explicitly note that the paper leaves it unstated.
The paper does not define "equivariant embedding" here; to make the question stand-alone, one should unpack it as a normal affine G-variety containing G as an open orbit.
The paper does not define "isotropy groups" here; to make the question stand-alone, one should say these are the point stabilizers G_x.

The exact meaning of "semisimple" for isotropy groups is not spelled out in the paper; a faithful rewrite should preserve the term rather than silently replace it by a stronger or different condition.
The equivalence notion for the classification is not stated explicitly; a stand-alone formulation should specify classification up to G-equivariant isomorphism.
It is useful to clarify that the problem ranges over connected solvable linear algebraic groups G, rather than fixing a single group G in advance.
refined_question: Fix a ground field k. Classify, up to G-equivariant isomorphism, all pairs (G, X) where G is a connected solvable linear algebraic k-group and X is a normal affine G-variety containing G as an open orbit (that is, a normal affine equivariant embedding of G), such that every point stabilizer G_x for x in X is semisimple; in particular, determine this classification in the special case where the maximal tori of G have dimension 1.
justification: The draft already captures the exact research target of the paper very closely: it is essentially the first sentence of Problem 4. The only paper-faithful sharpening needed is to unpack the standard embedding terminology so that the question is self-contained, to make the classification relation explicit, and to retain the paper's accompanying remark about the rank-one maximal-torus case. I did not add stronger hypotheses such as algebraic closure or characteristic-zero assumptions, because Problem 4 itself does not state them.
